name: Lutheran Kenoticism

phase_0.boundary_condition: The hypostatic union of the divine and human natures in the person of Christ

VINIT.justification: The unmanifest state of the Word before the incarnation event

TANCH.justification: The final enclosure where the divine attributes are fully integrated with the human form

AFWD.justification: The directed movement from the divine state toward the human condition

AREV.justification: The voluntary emptying or descent from the exercise of divine majesty

CLINK.justification: The sequential binding of divine and human natures into a single person

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-recognition of the Logos as remaining God even in the state of humiliation

FSPLIT.justification: The distribution of attributes where divine properties are shared with the human nature and human properties with the divine

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the single person from the distinct sets of shared attributes

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where the human nature exercises divine attributes

EVALF.justification: The state where the divine nature refrains from the use of its majesty

ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous presence of divine power and human suffering in the crucifixion

IFIX.justification: The irreversible historical fixation of the Word becoming flesh

phase_3.void_description: The silence of the Godhead before the economic revelation
phase_3.true_description: The state of glory and the full use of divine attributes
phase_3.false_description: The state of lowliness and the concealment of majesty
phase_3.both_description: The Lutheran paradox of the finite containing the infinite

steps.domain_action: The Logos exists in the eternal silence of the Father
The Logos identifies as the eternal and consubstantial Son
The Logos initiates the descent toward the finite creation
The conception occurs as a permanent entry into human history
The divine nature binds to the human nature in the womb
The single person branches into the communication of distinct attributes
The divine nature undergoes exinanition by choosing not to use its power
The state of humiliation is established in the earthly life of Jesus
The suffering on the cross holds both divine life and human death together
The resurrection affirms the human nature participating in divine glory
The attributes reconstitute the unified person of the ascended Christ
The Christ recognizes himself as the Lord of all creation
The system closes in the eternal session at the right hand of God

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Holy Spirit acting through the means of grace
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The genus idiomaticum facilitating the exchange of properties
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The Sacred Scriptures and the Book of Concord
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The divine economy of salvation history
phase_5.alfs_store: The Formula of Concord Article VIII

phase_6.cycle_cost: The voluntary veiling of the use of divine attributes
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The transcendent majesty of the Logos
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The immanent presence of the God-man in the Eucharist
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The divine essence remains undiminished despite the assumption of humanity
